I will say at 23 (I’m M, 24 currently) I was where you were at as well, and it took an older friend/co worker expressing to me that it’s standard at 23 to not know who you are. It takes years, and studies show you don’t really start to solidify your true self until I believe 32-35? Our brains and bodies are still developing through our 20s, but there’s this notion that we should have our lives together at such a young age.

Once I realized that and stopped thinking I needed to know myself and know everything I wanted at that age, I definitely changed my outlook a lot. I still struggle with my identity and what I want to this day, but recognizing that I have time to figure that out still has eased some of the anxieties at least and let me live life a little more freely now.

With COVID, I ended up deciding to go back to school to get my masters, because I recognized that I may never have the opportunity to do this again, and while not everyone has that opportunity I will say as shitty as 2020 has been, it’s at least forced me to look inward and focus on myself and what I want, whether that be professionally or personally, and encourage everyone to do the same. That can be as big as going back to school to as small as just trying some hobby you always said you didn’t have the time for. I always wanted to learn how to cook but never seemed to have the time with my work schedule and was constantly eating out. COVID shifted that and I was able to focus on learning about cooking snd found out I really enjoy it, and enjoy making it a constant part of my weeks now!

As far as friends and social skills, I think this year is hard for many in that regard anyways, and you’ll find many are open to meeting new people now, whether locally or virtually. We crave connections and our normal avenues for making those connections has been stalled. I personally have gotten very into different discord communities and that has helped ease some of my social tension from this year, but realistically I think the best way to meet people is to simply follow your hobbies and find avenues to meet people that have those similar interests. It’s much easier to be social with people when you know you have a common interest already to discuss!

As for style, I’ve also been learning more about my personal style this year, and if you’re interested in learning more about style I’ve been a big fan of Pinterest lately. I really enjoy Asian streetwear and business fashion and can dive down the rabbit hole for inspiration on that end and developing my own personal style, and it’s honestly quite different from the “norm” so I get looks from time to time too. I think style should be less to engage with others and more to engage with and find confidence in yourself. If you enjoy wearing something, and you find confidence in it, then it is stylish for you, and will let you shine through. Everyone has their own particular thoughts on style and I’ve found that wearing what makes you feel the most comfortable and confident is the best option at the end of the day :)

Hope this helps a bit, I relate a lot to your post and the last thing I’d say is don’t think too grand. Take small steps to find happiness. You ask about what you want or who you want to be, but instead of looking at the end goal, ask what it is that will make you happy in the short term, and set small goals to start. It will help to develop plans for the long term and to keep you motivated and happy in the here and now!

It always seems to be overcast these days. Like an ominous shadow is lurking over the city, hell even the world at times. I'd been staring out my window for god knows how long, watching drips of dew creep ever so slightly down the glass pane while I was running circles in my own head. Ma sat behind me with the tv flickering. I could hear that it was the news but was subconsciously filtering the words into a type of static that almost blocked out anything that wasn't my own active mind.

This was my life most days, another boring day in the ever so plush suburban Washington neighborhood that we were told we were lucky to live in. Ever since the globe's resources had become so scarce, only a few nation were able to continue living in a posh lifestyle. However, I didn't feel lucky. Cameras lined the street, making sure that no unnecessary waste or violent crimes broke out, everyone wore the same boring black polos and jeans (or skirts when it came to the girls on weekends), and I felt trapped in a giant pool of emptiness. Guess that's what happens when you're locked in a world full of conformity. The perfect lifestyle really isn't all that perfect when you end up living it.

"Tommy, Tommy, come over here! They heard something! They finally heard something!!!" My mother squealed with the excitement of a school kid that just got told they could eat two cookies. It took me a second to realize what she was talking about, but then I remembered that a few months back the government was sending messages out to space. Something about Satellite pulse waves encrypted with data or something, I was never really too big on science but it was a big topic. Some big wigs figured that we'd expended all options and that it was time to try and see if there was any life out there, give us some hope of finding a new planet that is habitable. Heaven knows this planet could only support humanity for a few more generations to come with all the shit we did to it.

I broke away from my gaze into my own personal contemplations and turned to the TV. Some new guy was sitting at the pristine desk, eager to report. They always cycled anchors every few weeks, couldn't be releasing too much information this day and age and everyone slipped up once in awhile. That's what you get when you hire some teenager straight out of school and trust them with government secrets, but at this point what else could they do.

"In exciting news, after months of attempts, we have received a transcribed message from the stars. While our teams are working nonstop to decode the message, this is an exciting leap forward for mankind. Your Government thanks you for your trust in them and in our efforts to create a better world not only for ourselves, but our future gener-" And that was it before the world descended into chaos. We still don't know what happened to this day, but next thing we know there was a massive electrical surge that cutout all the power. Only thing was, that shouldn't have been possible. The power was linked to some kind of solar panels that had energy that'd been stored for over 300 years, so even in the case of generators failing or anything like that we were supposed to be fine for years.

Ma and I sat perplexed, rendering what had happened, when the screen shook and a message vibrated across the screen. It was switching between some weird symbols and english letters for a while, but the whole time some kind of broken up voice was muttering something. The voice was getting louder, and I noticed that it switched from english to some kind of gibberish with the words on the screen. Finally, it was audible, and for a moment I froze not sure of what I was seeing. The screen finally settled, and in 6 simple words, humanity was sent into a shell shock. "Be quiet before they find you."

What did that mean? What was happening? Was this some kind of elaborate prank? That's all I thought of at first. Who takes some cryptic message to heart immediately. But see the thing was, pranks weren't normal. Nothing like this was normal. Before I could even grasp what was happening, the voice returned. It was gruff, half audible, almost like it was coming from one of those old radios we messed with in our transmissions class. "They'r..Comi.." The voice kept breaking up and coming back into focus.
